flows.title: 1 · Customer orders → request reaches drivers
flows.summary: The 4-step wizard creates the order in stage searching. A paired driver is offered first; otherwise eligible online drivers are offered one at a time, each with a response window.

flows.title: 2 · Driver accepts → everyone tracks the delivery
flows.summary: Accepting assigns the order and withdraws other open offers. All three apps follow the same order record.

steps.label: stage → assigned · dispatch accepted · others withdrawn

flows.title: 3 · Driver declines → record stays, next driver offered
flows.summary: The declined record and reason remain in the driver’s request history and the admin Driver requests tab. The customer keeps waiting.

steps.label: dispatch → declined · offer next eligible driver

flows.title: 4 · Driver misses the request → timeout
flows.summary: When the window passes without an answer, the next server tick marks the offer missed, notifies the driver and offers the order to the next driver.

flows.title: 5 · Multi-stop delivery with PIN handover
flows.summary: Each driver tap advances one stage; each stop is handed over with the recipient’s PIN or a confirmation. Apps converge within one poll (customer 2 s, admin 4 s).

flows.title: 6 · Payment after handover
flows.summary: Delivery creates a payment attempt. Uncertain results are checked before retrying. The payer can be the customer or the stop-1 recipient.

flows.title: 7 · Cash collection & remittance
flows.summary: For cash orders the driver records cash received, the payer confirms it, and finance records the platform-fee remittance. The driver’s retained earning is never paid twice.

flows.title: 8 · Driver releases an accepted delivery
flows.summary: Before loading, a driver can back out. The order returns to searching instead of being cancelled.

flows.title: 9 · Customer cancels
flows.summary: Allowed until cargo is collected. Open offers are withdrawn so drivers see why the request disappeared.

flows.title: 10 · Delivery messages
flows.summary: After acceptance, customer and driver exchange messages and quick replies on the order.

flows.title: 11 · Driver onboarding & approval
flows.summary: Drivers submit vehicle and four documents; staff review and approve, then the driver can go online.

flows.title: 12 · Operations reassigns a driver
flows.summary: Staff with trip access can assign any verified online driver with a suitable truck before cargo is collected.

flows.title: 13 · Driver payout request
flows.summary: Drivers request all scheduled earnings; finance approves and pays every included trip, or rejects with a reason.

flows.title: 14 · Live tracking across all three apps
flows.summary: Each driver stage update moves the truck on the customer map, the admin fleet map and the admin trip page within one poll (customer 2 s, admin 4 s). Positions are simulated from the stage.

flows.title: 15 · Operations manage a driver account
flows.summary: From the driver page, staff with “Edit, suspend and deactivate accounts” can set a driver offline, revoke verification, suspend, deactivate or reset a password. Each needs a reason and is audited.

steps.label: Open offers withdrawn · sessions revoked · audit

flows.title: 16 · Super Admin edits a role
flows.summary: Roles are records with permissions. Editing one changes what everyone in it can see and do on their next request; sections they lose are not rendered at all.

machines.title: Driver request (dispatch) outcomes
transitions: taken by another / cancelled / driver offline

sync: All three apps read one shared order record from the demo service.
Customer & Driver apps poll GET /snapshot every 2 s and on app foreground; Admin polls GET /admin every 4 s.
Mutations call refresh() immediately; a refresh requested during a poll is queued, not dropped.
Real-time = within one poll interval. Push/websockets are not implemented.
